ports.note: Every layer port, on every map, whatever its parameters say. The ports used to vary with an inputMode parameter -- reasoningInput, rasterInput, polygonInput, networkInput were four separate declarations of that -- so the port a connection needed might not exist on the node. Which renderer draws is now read from what is wired: src/core.ts#drawnMode.

ontology.note: Map presentation plan and MapView activity are implemented; broader map artifact and cartographic contracts remain open.

changes.description: A map declares every layer port it can draw and the practitioner wires what they have. The inputMode parameter no longer decides which ports exist, which presentation is offered or whether a basemap can be chosen; the renderer is read from the connections. The practitioner's direction of 2026-10-14 -- "there is no such thing as mode, only layers" -- which had been written into docs/widgets/map_output.md and into the layer vocabulary of the receipts while the interface kept asking the question.
changes.incompatibility: A map now has eight input ports instead of the two to four its mode allowed, so the node draws more handles and a canvas laid out around the old shape will look different. Saved workflows keep their inputMode value and nothing reads it except as a fallback for a map with nothing wired, so what they drew is what they draw. Anything that inspected a map's ports to infer its mode must read drawnMode instead.
changes.migration: None required for a saved workflow. The stored inputMode is read last and never written.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently.
